snippet.title: Why Haven't We Found Aliens Yet? The Fermi Paradox Explained | Orbit's Cosmic Journey
snippet.description:
Are we alone in the universe? The Fermi Paradox explained — if the Milky Way holds hundreds of billions of stars and countless planets, why does the sky stay so quiet?

In this Orbit's Cosmic Journey film, Orbit explores the Fermi Paradox, the Great Filter, the zoo hypothesis, the limits of interstellar communication, and how humanity might detect alien life. The first convincing sign may not be a spacecraft or a dramatic message. It may be a faint chemical fingerprint, an unusual pulse, or a clue already hidden inside old data.

CHAPTERS

The Fermi paradox asks why we have not encountered alien civilizations yet. Explore the vastness of space and the odds of life existing elsewhere.

This exploration examines the scale of the universe, from Earth's signal transmissions to the observation of distant galaxies. It breaks down the statistical likelihood of life on other planets and analyses why humanity has not made contact with extraterrestrial life despite the age of the universe.

Whether you are interested in astronomy or the search for life beyond Earth, this overview provides context on the current scientific perspective regarding the Fermi paradox. It details how signals travel through space and what we know about the potential for other civilisations among the stars.

Subscribe for weekly space science breakdowns, and comment below your theory on why we have not yet found alien life.

0:00 The Mystery of the Silent Sky
2:29 Enrico Fermi and the Paradox
4:51 The Drake Equation Explained
6:58 The Great Filter Theory
13:23 Searching for Techno-Signatures

What do you think explains the silence: distance, rarity, timing, deliberate quiet—or something we have not yet imagined?

Subscribe to Orbit for thoughtful space stories and big questions:
https://www.youtube.com/@OrbitWithBen

Wonder over certainty. Curiosity over clickbait.

snippet.title: What Happens Inside a Black Hole? (It's Not What You Think)
snippet.description:
What happens if you fall into a black hole? Join Orbit — a small orange exploration robot — on a black holes explained cosmic journey across the event horizon. In this space documentary we explore spaghettification, time dilation, the singularity, Hawking radiation, and what scientists still don't know about falling into a black hole.

🌌 Chapters:

Find out what happens inside a black hole if you were pulled in. We break down the physics of black holes and the fate of travellers.

This journey explores the extreme conditions awaiting anyone crossing the event horizon. We examine the reality of spaghettification and how gravitational forces would alter your physical form. If you have ever questioned the physics of black holes, this visual guide provides a clear look at these cosmic phenomena.

We also investigate the effects of time dilation black hole theories suggest, explaining how time itself behaves near such massive density. By the end of this video, you will understand exactly what happens inside a black hole, from the initial approach to the singular point, without the dry academic lecture.

Subscribe for weekly space science breakdowns, and tell us in the comments which cosmic mystery you want us to explore next.

0:00 The Reality of Falling In
0:40 Geometry of the Cosmic Dent
2:50 The Birth of a Black Hole
6:34 Simulating the Final Fall
8:57 Time Dilation and the Outside View
14:52 The Information Paradox

In this black hole documentary you'll learn:
• What the event horizon really is — and why it's the point of no return
• How time dilation would look from the outside vs from Orbit's cockpit
• Why spaghettification happens near a stellar-mass black hole
• What "inside a black hole" means for the singularity
• Black hole facts from Sagittarius A*, the Event Horizon Telescope, and gravitational waves

🪐 New cosmic journeys every week — subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
💬 Tell Orbit what to explore next in the comments.

This is an educational space documentary for curiosity, not fear. Science stays honest about what we know and what we don't (the information paradox, the exact interior).

snippet.title: Alien Worlds: The Strangest Planets We've Ever Found | Orbit's Cosmic Journey
snippet.description:
Alien worlds — Orbit visits the strangest planets we've ever found: diamond crusts, glass rain sideways, three suns, hot Jupiters, and eyeball exoplanets. Exoplanets explained as a space documentary cosmic journey.

What are alien worlds actually like? Diamond crusts. Glass rain sideways. Three suns in the sky. Hot Jupiters with nights that still glow. Eyeball planets locked between fire and ice.

Join Orbit — a small orange exploration robot — on Orbit's Cosmic Journey through the strangest planets in the universe. This is exoplanets explained the Orbit way: one world at a time, with the science we actually have… and the wonder we cannot help feeling.

In this space documentary we explore:
• What an exoplanet is (and why the catalogue is a museum of extremes)
• How we find alien planets — transit, stellar wobble, and atmospheric spectra
• Carbon-rich diamond worlds
• HD 189733 b–style glass rain and sideways weather
• Multi-star skies and triple shadows
• Hot Jupiters and the hottest nights in the data
• Tidally locked eyeball planets
• The habitable zone — and how we might one day smell life in a spectrum

Not fantasy. Measurements. Models. Honest uncertainty. Real wonder.
